Subject: SIG/CAIQ: request for IRP and short forensic snapshot (Nov 3 token anomaly)

Hi Sofia / Redwood security,

We observed a short-lived spike of invalid token usage against our integration on Nov 3 around 21:10 UTC. There were no confirmed exfiltration events, but our internal SecOps team would like to confirm containment and review IR artifacts to complete our SIG/CAIQ mapping for the customer audit next week.

Can you provide your incident response plan (IRP) summary for:
- containment and scope determination steps taken
- telemetry types available (auth logs, token rotation events, request traces)
- retention windows and redaction practices

We'd also like a short forensic snapshot (sanitized) containing:
- 24 hours of auth and token issue logs around the event
- redwood-side request IDs for any traffic from our tenant (Nov 3 20:00 - Nov 4 04:00 UTC)
- a brief timeline of actions taken by your on-call and any rollbacks or config changes

If possible, please flag anything that would need redaction before we attach the artifacts to our SIG export. We are under a compressed timeline for our auditor.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Senior Security Engineer, Novabank
Elaine.Park@novabank.com

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ: request for IRP and short forensic snapshot (Nov 3 token anomaly)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the sample form. We've started gathering the items you requested. High level:

- Containment: we rotated the tenant API key and applied a targeted deny rule for the affected token family at 21:28 UTC on Nov 3; no additional anomalous activity detected post-rotation.
- Telemetry: we can provide auth logs, request traces (token_id -> request_id mapping), and control-plane audit logs. Trace logs include request IDs and source IPs; network-level pcap is not retained.
- Retention & redaction: auth/request traces are retained for 90 days by default; we can produce a sanitized archive with IPs truncated and user PII redacted per your redaction checklist.

Planned deliverables (ETA Nov 5 16:00 PT):
1) short IRP executive summary (PDF) — containment timeline, owners, and mitigation steps
2) forensics snapshot (tar.gz) — logs + a manifest mapping request IDs to timestamps
3) redaction guidance doc — what we redact by default and how to request alternate redaction boundaries

Attachments we'll include: redwood_irp_exec_summary.pdf, forensics-snapshot-20261103.tar.gz (redacted).

If you need a stricter PII redaction (e.g., remove IPs entirely rather than truncation), let us know and we'll apply it before sharing.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Sofia / team — quick internal note before we hand artifacts to Novabank:

Proposed redaction defaults for customer-facing SIG artifacts (suggestions):
- IPs: truncate to /24 (e.g., 13.54.12.0/24) unless the customer requests full removal.
- User identifiers (internal IDs): replace with stable pseudonyms (user_001) and include crosswalk only in encrypted manifest.
- Sensitive URLs/keys: redact fully; provide request IDs and timestamps as linking keys.

Packaging: For the forensics tarball we'll include:
- manifest.csv (request_id,timestamp,service,redaction_flag)
- auth.log.gz (redacted)
- controlplane_audit.jsonl.gz (redacted)
- readme.txt (instructions + contact info)

Karthik — can you confirm retention export ranges and whether we can include the CIDR truncation in the packaged logs without breaking downstream parsers? Hannah — I'll need you to review the exec summary for operator-facing language.

Marissa
